svg.title: SSRF against the instance metadata service: IMDSv1 leaks credentials, IMDSv2 needs a session token and a hop limit
svg.text: SSRF to the metadata service
A web app that fetches user-supplied URLs can be made to call 169.254.169.254 from inside the instance.
IMDSv1 (simple GET)
Attacker
Vulnerable app
Metadata
1. ?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/...
2. A plain GET with no headers is enough.
3. The response (role credentials) flows back to the attacker.
Result: temporary role credentials stolen.
Fix: disable IMDSv1, require tokens; also fix the SSRF and shrink the role.
IMDSv2 (token required)
1. Client must first send PUT /latest/api/token with a TTL header.
2. Then GET with the token header on every request.
3. A GET-only SSRF cannot do step 1, so it gets 401.
4. Requests with X-Forwarded-For are rejected.
5. Hop limit 1: the token reply dies one network hop away,
so a container behind a bridge cannot get a token.
Result: the simple SSRF fails.
Azure: Metadata: true header. GCP: Metadata-Flavor: Google header.
These headers stop simple GET-only SSRF; a bug that lets the attacker
set headers defeats them. Defense in depth: egress filter, least privilege.
Behavior simplified; verify exact rules in provider documentation.
